items.title: 61531_Juan Tizol oral history interview
items.q: The interviewee mentions Stanley Dance only in the context of the interviewer referencing Dance's book or interviews ('in reading Stanley Dance's interview with you', 'I think it was Stanley Dance's book that mentions that'). There is no evidence of a direct personal relationship between Juan Tizol

ctx.x: Because he makes several references to you in the book. In Mercer's book, 'Duke Ellington in Person', by Mercer Ellington and Stanley Dance, Danna, they say, || In reference to Duke's composing, about his search for color and a technique that was more or less related to the art of painting. I don't know how much this matter of color related to dynamics, although Juan Tizol, who played valve trombone in the orchestra, always told me, 'Your papa likes to hear the

trombones play loud, and the trombones were always Pop's favorite section in the band. At one point, he was more interested in brass than anything else, and then quite suddenly, he seemed to become much more intrigued by the potential of the reed section.
